LayoutRules.title: Direction mapping
text: For LR, read left for top, right for bottom, top for left and bottom for right. BT and RL mirror TB and LR.

LayoutRules.title: One grid
text: Use one grid for the whole diagram. Every node sits on it, including diamond targets and group members.

LayoutRules.title: Box size
text: Draw every node in one box size. A diamond is the same width and twice the height. If the longest label does not fit, grow the box for every node by whole grid steps.

LayoutRules.title: Whole grid steps
text: Move nodes and grow gaps only in whole grid steps, across the whole rank or column. Never shrink a corner, straight run, label gap or padding to make something fit (see rank-gap-markup-2.png).

LayoutRules.title: Equal rank gaps
text: Make every rank gap equal to the base rank gap. A rank gap grows only to hold a label, a Z, extra tracks or a frame, and that growth changes no other gap (see rank-gap-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Snap to grid
text: Snap Mermaid's positions to the grid one whole rank or column at a time. If two nodes need the same place, push the second one 1 grid step on in rank order, and repeat until nothing overlaps.

LayoutRules.title: Always move forward (insert space)
text: Always move forward. Insert space only to meet a legality rule or to make room for a hint (rule 2.21): no overlap, and a track, a port slot and label room for every line. When a legality rule cannot be met in the space available, insert one whole grid step of space (rule 1.4) in the gap or rank concerned and apply the rule again. Stop when the gap holds every line and label it must carry; the amount needed is computed from them. No rule ends in a failure, and no rule depends on a diagram's size. Quality (crossings, shape, empty area) is decided by the score of rules 2.13 and 2.14, never by adding space.

LayoutRules.title: Start from Mermaid
text: Start from Mermaid's ranks and in-rank order, and change them only as rules 2.4 to 2.21 say, honoured hints (rule 2.21) first (rules 2.2 and 2.3 are pointers).

LayoutRules.title: Pointer to 2.18
text: See rule 2.18.

LayoutRules.title: Pointer to 2.17
text: See rule 2.17.

LayoutRules.title: Several parents
text: Put a node with several parents under its first parent that has no other child directly below it, taking parents in Mermaid's order. If every parent has one, keep the node's snapped column (1.6). Inside a 2.10 block, 2.10 decides which source a target sits under.

LayoutRules.title: Several children
text: If a node has several children, keep directly below it the child on the main path of rule 2.18 or, off the main path, the longest-path child (the child with the longest path to a node with no outgoing line). Place the other children as rule 2.17 sets: the next child goes as rule 2.17 sets.

LayoutRules.title: Detours and early exits
text: Put detours in the column next to the main path, in the ranks between the two main-path nodes they join. Put early exits in the column beyond the detours. Put both on the side of the main path where Mermaid placed most of them; on a tie, use the left side. A second branch from the same diamond goes on the opposite side.

LayoutRules.title: Diamond with loop child
text: When a diamond has two children, one on the main path and one starting a loop branch, keep the main-path child directly under the diamond (rule 2.18) and put the loop child in the next column, one rank lower, on the side Mermaid placed it. The main path continues straight (see wait-loop-markup.png, cycle-grid-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Chains through groups
text: A chain of nodes that each have one parent and one child stays in one column as it passes into and out of a group (see nested-chain-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Pointer to 2.10
text: See rule 2.10 (two-by-two is one case of it).

LayoutRules.title: Block of lines between two ranks
text: Block of lines between two ranks (any number of sources and targets). Within a rank, swap two nodes if that lowers the rule 2.13 score. When several sources in one rank link to several targets in the next rank, order the targets so that each sits under the source it has the most lines from (on a tie, the mean column of its sources, then Mermaid's order); that line drops straight down (rule 4.2). Every other line in the block leaves the bottom of its source and enters the top of its target, at ports spread across each side in the order that gives the fewest crossings (rules 3.2 and 3.3). Each line has its own track in the gap (rule 5.1). Lines cross only where no ordering of nodes, ports or tracks removes the crossing, and then at a right angle inside the gap (rules 5.6 and 5.9). No hops, side exits or runs along a frame. Grow the gap by whole grid steps until every line fits (rule 1.7) (see cross-links-markup.png, many-to-many-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Compaction
text: Compaction (applies in `grid`; `open` skips it). After honoured hints and rules 2.2 to 2.10, 2.15 to 2.18 and 2.20 (the order of rule 9.6), visit nodes in rank order and then left to right. Move each node up by whole rows and left by whole columns into the nearest free grid cell, so that it shares a row with its parent where the next cell is free (except a decision's side child, rule 2.17). Keep a move only if all of these hold: no box or frame overlaps; every line of the node still meets sections 3 to 5; the move gives a strictly lower rule 2.13 score; the node stays in the cell of rule 2.17, or in the column of one of its parents or beside it where rule 2.17 does not apply; and the move breaks no honoured hint (rule 2.21). After the initial placement is routed, also consider a coupled repair candidate when a crossing or hump can be removed by moving the affected unhinted node or group to any legal grid cell and reallocating the affected ports together. Reroute all affected lines and judge the complete candidate by its actual routes and score; keep it only under rules 2.13 and 2.14, and reject any candidate that breaks a hint or any other rule. A move that cannot lower the score is not retained. Compaction removes only rows and columns that hold no node, label, track or frame. It never shrinks a gap that holds a label, a Z, tracks or a frame (rule 1.4). The expected size of any compacted diagram is computed from the measured sizes of its nodes plus the gaps in these rules, and a test never hard-codes a pixel size. A node that belongs to a group stays in that group; a node that belongs to no group is not restricted. Passes repeat and the best layout is kept as set by rules 2.13 and 2.14. A cluster (rule 2.20) is one unit: it moves whole, by the same steps, and its nodes keep their places inside it. Rule 9.6 orders this rule against rules 2.15 to 2.18 and 2.20.

LayoutRules.title: Wrapping
text: Wrapping (applies in `grid`; `open` skips it). After rule 2.11, a row or column that is longer than the wrap length is wrapped. There is no fixed limit on nodes and no failure for size: a diagram of any size is wrapped for as many rows and columns as it needs. No honoured hint (rule 2.21) is broken.

- The wrap length is the number of nodes across, or down, that brings the whole diagram closest to 4:3 (width 4 parts to height 3 parts), without raising the rule 2.13 score. Never wrap a row or column that already fits within the wrap length. The shape is a ratio of the diagram's own computed size, with no fixed pixel size or node limit.

- Wide: cut a row longer than the wrap length into rows of at most that length. Draw the first nodes across, then start the next row directly under the previous row, in the same columns, one rank gap below.

- Deep: cut a column longer than the wrap length into columns of at most that length. Draw the first nodes down, then start the next column directly to the right of the previous column, one column gap away.
- Keep the order of the nodes: the next row or column continues from the node after the last one in the previous row or column.

- One line joins the pieces. For a wrapped row, it leaves the bottom of the far-right node, runs back along a track in the gap, and enters the top of the first node of the next row. For a wrapped column, it leaves the right side of the bottom node, runs along a track in the gap, and enters the left side of the first node of the next column. This line follows sections 3 to 5 like any other line.
- Wrapping never splits a group frame unless the group is itself longer than the wrap length. Nodes of one group stay together.

- After wrapping, run compaction (rule 2.11) again, so that wrapped rows and columns pack closer. A diagram can need both wide and deep wrapping. Compaction and wrapping repeat in passes; candidates are scored and kept, and the loop stops, as set by rules 2.13 and 2.14.
- The wrap length is counted in nodes of the standard box size (rule 1.3). Tests compute the expected size from measured node sizes and the gaps, and never hard-code a pixel size or a node limit.

LayoutRules.title: Layout score
text: Layout score. Every candidate layout of one diagram gets a score; lower is better. Score = shape + empty + crossings + bends + disconnected ends + hints. Shape: 2 points for every 5 percent the width-to-height ratio is away from 4:3 landscape (4 wide to 3 high), measured as a percentage of 4:3; too tall counts the same as too wide. Empty: the share of the diagram's bounding area not covered by node boxes, group frame and title space, labels or line tracks; 10 points for every 5 percent up to 30 percent, then 40 points for every 5 percent above 30 percent. Crossings: 20 points for every line crossing above the forced minimum; only crossings that no legal swap removes (rule 5.9) remain to be scored. The forced minimum is the fewest crossings that the diagram's links make unavoidable. For a complete block of n boxes linked to m boxes in two adjacent ranks it is n(n-1)/2 times m(m-1)/2. Elsewhere it is the number of pairs of lines that cross in every possible order, or zero when that cannot be shown. Crossings up to the forced minimum score no points but are still reported. Bends: 10 points for every corner on a line. Disconnected ends: 20 points for each source or destination end of a drawn line that does not meet its box or group outline; legend samples are excluded. Hints: see rule 2.21(g). Shape, empty and crossing points are prorated between steps. An overlap, or any line that breaks sections 3 to 5, rejects the candidate; it gets no score. The score only compares layouts of the same diagram; it is never a pass mark and never a size limit. Tests compute scores from the measured layout and never hard-code a pixel size.

LayoutRules.title: Keep the best
text: Keep the best. Compaction and wrapping (rules 2.11 and 2.12) produce candidates. Keep a candidate only if its score is strictly lower than the best so far. Stop when a full pass finds no lower score, or when a pass repeats an earlier layout. Then return the best layout found. The engine never fails or gives up because of diagram size or pass count. The 30 percent empty figure is a goal and a score step (rule 2.13), not a limit. The goal is no needless crossings (crossings above the forced minimum) and under 30 percent empty; a diagram that ends above 30 percent reports its empty share and the reason, and this is not a failed attempt.

LayoutRules.title: Unconnected pieces
text: Unconnected pieces. Nodes, or small connected pieces, that have no line to other pieces (inside one group or in the whole diagram) are arranged as a block of rows and columns in declared order, left to right and then top to bottom, sized by the wrap length of rule 2.12. The group frame grows to fit the block. Pieces in a group stay in that group. A cluster (rule 2.20) is one piece and is placed whole.

LayoutRules.title: Fans
text: Fans. When one node has lines to or from many nodes on one side (a fan, one-to-many or many-to-one), the many nodes wrap into rows sized by the wrap length of rule 2.12, with the single node centred beside the block. Lines are routed as rule 5.8 sets; lines of inner rows may also use the gaps between rows and between boxes of outer rows as further nested tracks (rule 5.2). No avoidable crossings and no hops (rule 5.9).

LayoutRules.title: Under the parent
text: Under the parent. A node whose main link is to one parent is placed directly under that parent (or, in a left-to-right flow, to its right), centred on it, when that grid cell is free. Compaction (rule 2.11) keeps this cell or, when it is taken, the cell beside the parent. When the cell under the parent is taken by another child, the next child of a decision goes in the next column one rank lower (rule 3.8); the next child of any other node goes beside the parent on the parent's row, so its line is straight. If that cell is taken, use the nearest free cell. The only child of a node goes directly under it in the same way, unless rule 2.4 places that child under another parent.

LayoutRules.title: Main path
text: Main path. The main path is the path of least resistance: the route a reader's eye follows. Start at a node with no incoming line. At each node follow its one outgoing line when it has only one; at a decision, follow the branch with the longest decision-free run, with Mermaid's source order breaking a tie; where several flows converge, the converging node is on the main path of the strongest of them, the one that carries the longest decision-free run. Node labels and edge-label words never choose the path. Stop at a node with no outgoing line or one already on the path. Nodes on the main path share one centre line along the flow, so lines between them are straight (rule 4.7), except where a hint (rule 2.21) places the node. The main path never moves sideways to make room (see main-spine-markup.png). A node with one parent sits under that parent (rule 2.17); other nodes sit beside the main path. A node where flows converge is centred under (or beside) the main-path node that feeds it, and the other feeding lines enter as rule 4.11 sets. This rule outranks rule 2.11 for nodes on the main path: compaction never moves a main-path node off the centre line. Where a node with one parent hangs off a main-path node, rule 2.17 decides its place. Inside a 2.10 block the main path keeps its straight column; 2.10 orders the other targets around it.

LayoutRules.title: Free direction
text: Free direction. When a diagram declares no direction, the engine tries each flow direction (down, right, up, left) and keeps the layout with the lowest score (rules 2.13 and 2.14), so a simple chain comes out as a straight run with the fewest corners. When a direction is declared, it is used and not changed. Hints (rule 2.21) apply inside the direction in use and never change a declared direction; with none declared, each trial scores its own honoured hints. There is no size threshold: the same rule applies to small and large diagrams. Each trial applies rule 1.1 to its direction, and Mermaid's ranks are recomputed for it. Trials may run in parallel and reuse results.

LayoutRules.title: Clusters
text: Clusters. A cluster is a set of nodes in which the share of possible links that exist inside the set is higher than the share between the set and the rest of the diagram. Find clusters from the links alone. A cluster never crosses a group frame, and every node is in at most one cluster. A node with no cluster is a cluster of one. Placement, compaction (rule 2.11), wrapping (rule 2.12), unconnected pieces (rule 2.15) and the 4:3 shape (rule 2.13) treat each cluster as one unit and move it whole. Inside a cluster, the nodes keep the order that gives the fewest crossings. A cluster linked to another cluster faces it, rank against rank, and the lines between them follow the many-to-many rule. A cluster longer than the wrap length is wrapped as a whole by rule 2.12, with its inner order unchanged. A cluster that contains a hinted node keeps that hint (rule 2.21): the cluster moves whole with the hinted node's peer relation intact; a hint that would split a cluster across a frame is a legality case (a group frame never holds a non-member, rule 7.3) and is handled as rule 2.21(f) sets; in every other case the cluster moves whole around the hinted node.

LayoutRules.title: Hints
text: Hints. A node, a group or a line may carry a hint on its own declaration line, so that a diagram can keep the structure of an original. A hint overrides automatic placement as the preamble sets. Hints are used as follows.

- (a) Written: a node or group hint is words at the end of its declaration line: above, below, left-of or right-of a named peer, optionally followed by an offset +n; or push N, S, E or W. A line hint is written in square brackets after the relationship: leave N|S|E|W, enter N|S|E|W, travel N|S|E|W, separated by commas. N, S, E and W are screen directions and are never rotated by rule 1.1.

- (b) Meaning: "above P" or "below P" puts the node in the same column as P, and "left-of P" or "right-of P" puts it in the same row, on that side, in the nearest free cell. With an offset +n it is exactly n cells further when that cell is free, otherwise the next free cell further on (+0 is the adjacent cell). "push D" puts the node in the extreme free cell in direction D inside its own group, or inside the diagram when it has no group. "leave D" and "enter D" name the side of the source box and of the target box that the line uses. "travel D" is the direction of the middle (track) run of the line; a straight line has no middle run, so travel on it is not honoured.

- (c) Peers: a peer must be a node or group at the same level, in the same group. Any other peer (missing, or in another group) means the hint is ignored and reported. When the peer is in another cluster (rule 2.20), the two clusters are placed relative to each other as the hint says. A hint that would split a cluster across a frame is a legality case (group frames never hold non-members, rule 7.3): it is not honoured under (f), and it is reported.

- (d) Order and conflicts: take hints in source order and add each to the set. A hint that would make the set impossible (for node and group hints, a circle of peers; for line hints, two lines hinted to the same port on one box side) is dropped and reported, and the earlier hints stay. Two nodes hinted to the same cell are not a conflict: the later one takes the next free cell further on, on that side (as in (b)), and its hint is still honoured.
- (e) Hinted nodes keep their relation to their peer and move together with it; rules 2.11, 2.12, 2.15 and 2.20 never break an honoured hint (a cluster moves whole around a hinted node).

- (f) Legality: a hint never overrides legality (overlaps, section 10, room for lines); it does override the routing faults list after section 10. Space is inserted as rule 1.7 sets, to make room for a hint. A hinted line may use the corners its hint needs, without the corner limit of rule 4.3; its corners are still scored (rule 2.13).

- (g) Score: each honoured node or group hint scores -30 and each honoured line hint scores -15 in rule 2.13, so honoured hints may outweigh a few crossings. The score only compares candidates; it never drops an honoured hint. This is intended: the structure of an original is preferred to calculated layout. A hint that cannot be honoured earns nothing, is reported with the reason, and layout continues; nothing fails.
- (h) Direction: see rule 2.19. A node, group or line without a hint is laid out as before.

LayoutRules.title: Notes
text: Notes. A note is a free-text box with a dog-ear corner. It is not an ArchiMate element and has no relationship meaning. It may sit in a group or at the top level. For layout a note is a box like a node: its size comes from its text (grown by whole grid steps, rule 1.3), it sits on the grid, rules 2.4 to 2.20 place it, it takes a node hint and a group (rule 2.21), and its lines use ports as rule 4.7 sets. By default a note sits beside the node or group it connects to, on that row in the nearest free cell (as rule 2.17 sets for a child beside its parent); a note with no connection is an unconnected piece (rule 2.15). A plain connection (rule 4.10) is not a relationship, so a note is not a relationship end: it does not count in the forced minimum (rule 2.13) or in cluster detection (rule 2.20, which uses relationships only). A text that sits on a line is not a note: it is the label of that line (rules 6.1 and 6.2).

LayoutRules.title: One port per line
text: Use one port per line, so lines never share a port or a first run. A line meets its port at a right angle and ends exactly on the drawn outline (see f11-straight-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Symmetric port allocation
text: Allocate all lines on a box side together, not one line at a time. For n lines, place n ports at positions k/(n+1) of the side length, for k=1 to n, measured from left to right or bottom to top. This makes one line use the centre; odd counts include the centre and mirrored pairs, and even counts use mirrored pairs straddling the centre. Assign lines to the ports in target order (rule 3.3). Thus two lines use the thirds, three use the quarters, four use the fifths, and five use the sixths. There is no fixed port or line maximum. If the ports or their first runs do not fit legally, grow the box along that side by whole grid steps (rules 1.3 and 1.7), then recompute the same symmetric positions.

LayoutRules.title: Port order
text: On each side, order the ports by where each line's other end is, so no two lines cross next to the node.

LayoutRules.title: Removed
text: Removed; see 4.8.

LayoutRules.title: Removed
text: Removed; see 4.8.

LayoutRules.title: Diamond ports
text: A decision diamond always has its four vertices as ports and at least three further ports evenly spaced along each of its four edges: at least 16 ports in total. For n active ports on one edge, place them at the n equal interior divisions: one at the half, two at the thirds, three at the quarters, four at the fifths, and so on. Keep at least the three quarter-point candidates available and add as many evenly distributed ports as required; there is no fixed maximum. Reassign all lines on that edge together: preserve their destination order so they do not cross beside the diamond, then choose the distinct ports with the least total displacement; later routing and crossing repair judge the complete routes by their real crossing count. A forward line enters at the top vertex, unless a line hint (rule 2.21) names another vertex or side. Branches take vertices first (rule 3.8). Further incoming lines use the free side vertices, then the ports along the upper edges. When the diamond needs more room to keep those ports and their first runs separate, grow it by whole grid steps (rules 1.3 and 1.7).

LayoutRules.title: Straight branch below diamond
text: A branch to a target directly below the diamond leaves the bottom vertex as a straight line.

LayoutRules.title: Decision branches
text: Decision branches. With two or three branches, the outer branches leave from the diamond's left and right vertices and the middle branch (the main-path branch when there are two and one target is directly below) from the bottom vertex. A branch whose target is lower and in another column leaves the side vertex facing it horizontally, uses exactly one corner, and runs straight down to the target, entering as rule 4.11 sets. A branch never leaves from a diamond position that is not a vertex. If the facing vertex is taken, or its run before the corner would be shorter than the minimum straight run, insert space as rule 1.7 sets (legality) and route again (see decision-accepted.png, merge-decision-markup.png, pictures/markup-decision-branches.png, pictures/markup-three-way-decision.png).

LayoutRules.title: No sideways turn from bottom vertex
text: Never leave the bottom vertex and then turn sideways, unless a line hint (rule 2.21) names another vertex or side. Two branches to mirror-image targets are mirror images (see decision-three-way-markup.png, pictures/markup-three-way-decision.png).

LayoutRules.title: Arrowhead and cross-marker boundary
text: Arrowhead tips end exactly on the visible shape outline and never overlap or cross into the box. A cross endpoint marker keeps the exterior clearance in parameter cross_endpoint_standoff; its line ends at the marker anchor, outside the box.

LayoutRules.title: Straight runs and corners only
text: Build every line from straight runs and corners only. No diagonals, S-curves, free curves or hop arcs.

LayoutRules.title: Aligned ports are straight
text: When the ports line up on one column or row line, draw a single straight run, whatever the two shapes' sizes, unless a line hint (rule 2.21) says otherwise.

LayoutRules.title: Corner limit
text: A line has at most 2 corners, 3 for a back edge; insert space until met (rule 5.7). A line with a hint (rule 2.21) may use the corners its hint needs. A line never loops on itself, and never runs past the side of its target that faces the source and turns back.

LayoutRules.title: Minimum straight run at ends
text: Every line runs straight for at least the minimum straight run after leaving its source and before its arrowhead, so no corner sits closer than that to either end.

LayoutRules.title: Z middle run on a track
text: Put a Z's middle run on a track in the gap between the source and target ranks (see lr-fanout-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: No running along outlines
text: A line never runs along a node outline or a frame edge. It crosses a frame only at a right angle. A line to or from a group follows rule 4.9.

LayoutRules.title: Port placement
text: Port placement. Allocate all automatic lines on each side together by rule 3.2, then assign the symmetric ports in target order so that no line runs back past another. A single line uses the centre port and is straight when its opposite port also lies on the same row or column line (rule 4.2). With multiple lines, do not reserve the centre for one line and leave the rest on only one side: an odd-sized set has a centre port and mirrored pairs, while an even-sized set has mirrored pairs straddling the centre. A legal line hint (rule 2.21) that names a side fixes that line to the named side; include it when allocating that side's ports. Port allocation is joint across routes: when a new port choice would create a crossing or a renderer hump, reallocate the affected ports together, including ports already assigned to the other lines, and reroute those lines. Keep the symmetric sets and all hints, and choose among legal assignments by the real crossing count after routing (rules 5.6 and 5.9). An end marker sits on the port and takes no extra room.

LayoutRules.title: Fewest corners
text: Fewest corners. A line leaves and enters the sides that give it the fewest corners: none when the centres align (rule 4.7), otherwise one, by leaving the side that faces the target and entering the target on the side that faces the source. When two choices have the same number of corners, the one along the flow direction wins. A line never uses a side that makes it cross a box. A line leaves a side only when the other end lies wholly beyond that side. A Z is used only when no one-corner route is clear; its middle run is on a track (rule 4.5). A legal line hint (rule 2.21) that names a side overrides this choice.

LayoutRules.title: Group endpoints
text: Group endpoints. A relationship may name a group as its source or its target. The endpoint is the group's frame, and the frame is treated as a box in rules 3.1 to 3.3, 4.2, 4.4, 4.7, 4.8, 5.1 to 5.6 and 2.13, and in line hints (rule 2.21): the line leaves or enters the frame on the side that faces the other end, at a port allocated symmetrically by rules 3.2 and 4.7, square-on to the frame. The line starts or ends on the outer edge of the frame and never begins inside it, except a line between a group and one of its own members, which meets the inner edge of the frame and crosses nothing else needlessly. A line to a group never runs along the frame edge. A frame endpoint that needs more ports or tracks adds room as rule 1.7 sets (legality).

LayoutRules.title: Plain connection
text: Plain connection. A plain connection is an undirected line, with no arrowheads and no relationship type, between a note and a node or group, or between two notes. It is drawn like any other line: sections 3 to 5 apply, a group end follows rule 4.9, its corners and crossings are scored by rule 2.13, and it may carry a line hint (rule 2.21). It is not a relationship and never enters the model.

LayoutRules.title: Convergence
text: Convergence. When several lines enter one target, a line from a source directly above the target enters its top as one straight run (rule 4.2). A line from a source in another column, including a diamond branch (rule 3.8), uses one corner (rule 4.8): it enters the top centre port when that port is free; otherwise it runs straight along the flow to the target's row and enters the side of the target that faces the source. A converging line never runs along the gap above the target to reach its top, and never enters the top with an S-jog (two corners), unless a line hint (rule 2.21) names that route. Lines inside a block of rule 2.10 follow rule 2.10 instead; this side entry applies only to lines from outside such a block (see pictures/markup-merge-into-end.png, pictures/markup-merge-into-end-detail.png, pictures/markup-merge-finish.png).

LayoutRules.title: One line per track
text: Two lines never use the same track where their runs overlap. If a gap has fewer free tracks than lines, insert space as set by rule 1.7 and route again.

LayoutRules.title: Fan nesting
text: In a fan, the line to the node furthest out takes the outermost track and port, and the line to the nearest node takes the innermost. Apply this to fan-out and fan-in, and to both halves of the fan (see fan-nesting-markup.png). Fans between columns follow rule 5.8.

LayoutRules.title: Back-edge sides
text: A back edge leaves its source's downstream side if that side is free; if not, it leaves the side facing its return track. It enters the middle of the target's side that faces the return track (see loop-back-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Return track side and order
text: Put the return track on the same side of the main path as the back edge's source. If the source is on the main path, use the side with no branches; if that is still tied, use the right side. When several back edges share a side, the longest takes the outermost track.

LayoutRules.title: Removed
text: Removed; see 2.10.

LayoutRules.title: Joint reassignment before accepting
text: Before accepting a route, reassign the tracks, ports or sides of the affected lines together, including other lines that share their ports or tracks, if that removes a crossing (rule 5.9), then if it lowers the rule 2.13 score. If port reassignment alone cannot remove an avoidable crossing or hump, consider the coupled unhinted node or group move in rule 2.11, then reallocate ports and reroute. Reroute every affected line and judge the actual crossing count and complete score. A crossing that remains is allowed only at a right angle inside a gap, and is scored by rule 2.13.

LayoutRules.title: Insert space until legal
text: If no route meets every legality rule, insert space for legality rules, or to make room for a hint (rule 2.21), as rule 1.7 sets, in the gap or rank concerned and route again. Nothing is reported as failed, and there is no size or pass limit. Never draw a tangle.

LayoutRules.title: Fans between columns
text: Fans between columns. When lines fan out from one source to targets that lie wholly beyond its left or right side, or fan in to one target from such sources, each line leaves the side of the source that faces the target and enters the side of the target that faces the source, at spread ports (rules 3.2 and 3.3). Each line has its own track in the gap between the columns, and the tracks are nested as rule 5.2 sets so that the lines do not cross each other. A fan line never leaves the source's far side, top or bottom to go round the source, never enters at a box corner, and never shares a track with another fan line, unless a line hint (rule 2.21) names the side. Fans to the next rank use the bottom and top sides (rules 2.10 and 5.2). Insert space for the tracks as rule 1.7 sets (see pictures/markup-fan-out-bad.png, which shows what is forbidden).

LayoutRules.title: Avoidable crossings
text: Avoidable crossings. For a block of lines between sibling group boundaries, apply the node and port ordering in rule 2.10 first. A crossing that a different track, port or side assignment removes, while keeping every other rule of sections 3 to 5 (including the corner limit of rule 4.3) and every line hint, is a fault: the route is rejected and that assignment is used. A crossing that no such assignment removes stays as a plain right-angle crossing (rule 5.6) and is scored (rule 2.13). Hops are never drawn (rule 4.1) (see pictures/markup-fan-out-bad.png).

LayoutRules.title: Label on a straight run
text: Centre each label on a straight run of its own line, on a white background, with the line broken round it and one label gap on each side (see edge-label-markup.png). The line keeps its own course through the label: it is never bent, jogged or moved sideways to make room for a label, and a label never sits on a corner. If no straight run is long enough, insert space as rules 1.7 and 6.2 set (label room is legality) (see pictures/markup-decision-branches.png, pictures/markup-three-way-decision.png).

LayoutRules.title: Label run choice
text: Use the longest straight run that holds the label and both label gaps clear of every corner and arrowhead. On a tie, use the run nearer the source. If no run is long enough, grow the gap it crosses by whole grid steps.

LayoutRules.title: Node label centred in its box
text: Centre every node's label horizontally and vertically inside its visible box. Measure the rendered label bounds; neither the text baseline nor an icon changes the centring point.

LayoutRules.title: Title strip
text: Never cover or shorten the title strip. If the title is wider than the members, widen the frame by whole grid steps.

LayoutRules.title: Members on grid
text: Members stay on the shared grid. If a frame needs more room, grow the whole rank gap or column gap; never move a member off its grid line.

LayoutRules.title: No frame overlap
text: Frames never overlap each other or cross a node that is not a member. When two frames, or a frame and an outside node, sit in neighbouring columns or ranks, grow that gap by 1 grid step, or by 2 when a line also runs through it (see frame-overlap-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Centre lone nested group
text: Centre a group across its parent group when it is the only group nested in that parent.

LayoutRules.title: Back edge inside group
text: If both ends of a back edge are members of a group, keep its return track inside that group's frame.

LayoutRules.title: Member inset
text: Keep at least one grid step between a frame outline and every member node on all four sides, below the title band. Grow the frame or its surrounding gap in whole grid steps; never move a member off-grid.

LayoutRules.title: Centre group members
text: Centre a group's member layout within its frame horizontally and vertically when the group has no placement hint. An honoured hint (rule 2.21) determines the placement and takes precedence.

LayoutRules.title: Sequence notes
text: Leave the same clear space above and below a note as between two consecutive messages. A note never touches a message line, an arrowhead or a label. Set this in the shared row layout, never for one diagram (see sequence-note-markup.png).

LayoutRules.title: Legality first
text: Never break an item in section 10. If a layout would break a legality item, insert space for legality rules, or to make room for a hint (rule 2.21), as rule 1.7 sets, and route again; a quality item (crossings, shape, empty area) is settled by the score of rules 2.13 and 2.14, not by space.

LayoutRules.title: Grow space before breaking legality
text: Before breaking a legality rule, grow the gap concerned by whole grid steps and route again, as rule 1.7 sets. Space is never grown for quality.

LayoutRules.title: Specific beats general
text: A specific rule beats a general one within one step of rule 9.6: diamond rules (3.6 to 3.9) beat box rules (3.1 to 3.3, 4.7 and 4.8), and back-edge rules (5.3 to 5.4) beat forward-line rules. Hints rank above all of these (see the preamble).

LayoutRules.title: Tie-break order
text: Within rules 2.11 to 2.21, candidates are compared only by the score of rule 2.13, except that an honoured hint (rule 2.21) is kept; the order below applies to the routing and placement choices inside one candidate. Otherwise the earlier item in this list wins: (1) one grid and whole grid steps; (2) placement (section 2); (3) ports and line shape (sections 3 and 4); (4) fewer crossings; (5) fewer corners; (6) label position; (7) Mermaid's original rank and order.

LayoutRules.title: Mermaid order on tie
text: If a choice is still tied, keep Mermaid's order.

LayoutRules.title: Precedence
text: Precedence. Hints: see the preamble and rule 2.21. Placement: honoured hints (2.21) first; then 2.18; then 2.7 (compatible with 2.18, as it keeps the main path straight); then 2.4 to 2.6 and 2.8 to 2.10 (rule 2.4 applies within this step, so a child that rule 2.4 places under another parent is placed there, not by 2.17); then 2.17, 2.16, 2.20 and 2.15; then compaction 2.11 (which keeps the cell of 2.17); then wrapping 2.12; then 2.19 picks among the resulting candidates by score and never overrides a declared direction. Routing: line hints (2.21); then 4.7; then 3.8, 4.11 (lines inside a 2.10 block follow 2.10) and 5.8; then 4.8; then 5.9 (within 4.3 and the line hints). After this initial placement and routing, the coupled repair in rules 2.11 and 5.6 may revisit an unhinted node or group together with its affected ports; it must keep every higher-priority placement rule and hint. The routing faults list yields only to line hints. A higher item is never moved by a lower one. Section 10 items and overlaps are never broken. Ties go to Mermaid's order (9.5).

LayoutParameters.source: Terms: Straight run (corner radius + 1 grid step); decision 2

LayoutPrecedence.name: Grid and measured geometry (prerequisite of every stage; not named in 9.6)
Multi-parent, branches, detours, chains, blocks (2.4 applies within this step)
Parent placement, fans, clusters, unconnected pieces
Free direction picks among candidates by score (never overrides a declared direction)
Decision branches, convergence (2.10 block lines follow 2.10), fans between columns
Avoidable crossings (within 4.3 and the line hints)
Coupled node/group repair after initial placement and routing
Labels, frames and sequence notes (not named in 9.6)
Legality: section 10 and overlaps never broken; ties go to Mermaid order (9.5)
